triage_agreement.server_py_662_embed_script: AGREE — line 662 emits <script src='.../embed.js' data-token='{preview_token}'> and preview_token is a per-tenant PUBLIC token (already exposed on /p/{token} and /site-admin/{token} in test_credentials.md). It is NOT a secret; no fix needed.
triage_agreement.page_guard_edit_requests_circular_import: AGREE — verified: page_guard.py:35 does `from edit_requests import active_grant` INSIDE a function, and edit_requests.py:53 does `from page_guard import role_of` INSIDE a function. Both modules are wired at module load from server.py (lines 1008-1011) with no module-level cycle. This is the textbook cycle-break pattern.
triage_agreement.ruff_F821_F811_E711_E712: AGREE — `ruff check --select F821,F811,E711,E712 /app/backend` reports 'All checks passed!'. No undefined names, no redefinitions, no `== None` or literal `== True/False` comparisons in scope. The remaining `is False` uses are deliberate None-vs-False tri-state checks and are correct.
triage_agreement.silent_catch_fixes: VERIFIED — Dashboard.jsx line 65 now logs `console.warn('Could not load notifications', ...)`; AuthContext.jsx line 43 now logs `console.warn('Logout request failed, clearing the session locally', ...)` before `setUser(null)`. Both are the minimum-diff fixes described.

issues: Dashboard.jsx line 187 calls `nav("/")` after logout but the observed URL ends up on `/login` instead of the marketing landing page — Landing likely redirects unauthenticated visitors. Behaviour is functionally correct (session is cleared, user can re-login) but does not literally match the task's 'lands on the landing page' phrasing.

A short burst of ~10 React 'Maximum update depth exceeded' warnings fires in the console during the logout → /login transition. Login page renders normally and re-login succeeds, but this indicates a probable useEffect dep-array smell in Landing or a page-transition wrapper (not in the two files touched this iter). Pre-existing, not caused by this fix. Worth investigating separately.

action_items: (Optional, not blocking) Investigate the transient 'Maximum update depth exceeded' console errors during the logout→/login transition — most likely a useEffect dep-array issue in Landing.jsx or a route-transition wrapper.
(Cosmetic) Confirm whether nav('/') after logout should stay on the landing page or intentionally bounce to /login; adjust Dashboard.jsx line 187 or Landing.jsx redirect accordingly.
critical_code_review_comments: Dashboard.jsx loadNotifs fix is correct — console.warn on failure preserves the working-app UX (bell still opens, dropdown just shows 'No activity yet') without swallowing the error.
AuthContext.jsx logout fix is correct — the local session is always cleared even if POST /auth/logout errors, and the warning is emitted first with status/message. This is the right ordering.

Triage of the code-quality report is accurate: the three big-ticket items (embed 'secret', circular import, undefined vars) are all false positives, and the hook-dep / index-key / component-size items are refactors of working code with no observable symptom — deferring them is defensible.
